Using competitor intel to optimize your game ad creatives
Tomas Hubka
Last updated: Aug 28, 2026
min read
With limited third-party tracking, game marketing teams need meaningful data and better ways to analyze competitor strategies and creative performance.
Ad Insights
, the competitive intelligence tool inside MarketIQ Pro, helps bridge this gap by offering clear insights into what's working across formats, platforms, networks, and audiences. UA managers get the metrics they need for data-backed decisions, and game marketers get insights on trends and creative strategies to keep campaigns fresh and engaging.
As competition is fierce, marketers are hyper-focused on ROAS and want metrics that deliver high-performing campaigns without wasting spend. Ad Insights makes this easier by allowing you to efficiently compare ad performance, analyze top creatives, and spot trends across networks, cutting down on time spent while keeping results high. The need for creative inspiration and access to data that shows how different creatives capture attention has been inaccessible to most teams. With Ad Insights, you can dive into leading creative examples and understand what users respond to, shaping ads that are both targeted and impactful.
There isn't just one correct way to use Ad Insights. Through exploring the tool, you'll find numerous ways to leverage the insights this platform provides. But if you're just getting started and looking for guidance, consider this your ultimate guide to exploring what works and what doesn't in the mobile game advertising realm.
Developing and operating a game is no different from running a business. As such, you naturally have competitors, whether you know of them or not. Using Ad Insights will help you look under the cover of your competition's advertising strategies and outsmart them in the best possible way. With this in mind, the two use case scenarios we're exploring today are:
I know my competition and want to perform better than them
I need help understanding the competitive landscape for my game
Let's jump right in. Here is your 101 guide to optimizing your creatives.
Know your competition like the back of your hand
To understand how your competitors behave in the advertising space, replicate the following steps:
Search for the game.
Navigate to the search bar and type the game name you're looking for. Depending on the platform, you'll see an option for iOS and/or Android (you can switch platforms as you continue exploring). Click the one you want to examine and add it to your
Favorites (❤️)
so you can revisit it easily.
Open Creative Insights.
After selecting your game, you're automatically directed to
Creative Insights
, which shows you all creatives across all ad networks and regions. In this overview, you can see the total number of ads that your competitor is running across all regions, their types (playable, video, or image), as well as a high-level overview of ad platforms and KPIs.
Filter to the segment that matters to you.
There are many ways to use the filtering and sorting options to find exactly what you need. Let's say you want to distribute your game to Canada, your preferred creative type is video, and you want to target the English-speaking Canadian population. Simply input these values into the filters and hit
OK
. The results show how your competitor advertises their game in this region, using video to appeal to their English-speaking audience. You can then sort the results by discovery time, ad duration, impression estimate, or a specific engagement metric, whichever metric you're expecting to improve.
Note: if you don't see any results, it's possible your competitor wasn't advertising in the selected period. Try adjusting the period to further past. If you still don't see any results, it's likely that your competitor doesn't cover this region. While you might see this as an opportunity, we suggest exploring other competitor and genre performances in the region first, as the audience may simply not be there.
Study individual ads in detail.
Once you've found the results you're looking for, let's see what valuable data each ad snippet includes. To open the card, click on the
Detail
button represented by a paper
